summary: Normalize negative system-time remainders to the preceding second.
explanation: The current formatter treats a zero remainder as negative and adjusts it by only half a second. For the epoch `tp`, this makes `{:%M:%S}` produce `59:59.500000` instead of `00:00.000000`; the alignment variants show the same incorrect value with padding. For negative fractional timestamps, adding only half a second also leaves a negative subseconds value, causing the wrong fractions reported for `epoch - d` and the nanoseconds-minimum contract. The `timestamp_ratios` assertions likewise show incorrect second and date fields for `t3`, `t4`, and `tp`; the `timestamp_sub_seconds` assertions show incorrect seconds or fractions for `t5`, `t9`, `epoch - d`, and `epoch`. Adjust only strictly negative remainders: move the calendar time back one second and add one full second to the remainder. A zero remainder then stays at the epoch, while negative fractions become nonnegative without unsigned conversion of a negative subseconds value.
